body:
The orchestrator is now counted as the orchestrator from what it does (it launches, lands, runs its own resume), so a session that starts with a question or takes over mid-way is no longer "other". A part's first look at the board now reads only its own post, its comments and the cards (6 times less text), and reading a whole collection by hand is refused before it runs, for every session. A new audit lists, session by session, each time someone did by hand what a kit command does, with the command to use; the orchestrator sees the top 3 in its resume.

### What he asked
In chat, 2026-11-26 (no comment id: the step's source): "make a step to fix the role label and full board pulls; check sessions used the kit's commands". Answered by bars 1, 2 and 5; reply-36c163cac42c by bars 3 and 4.

### What was wrong
- **The label.** 9919b5f1 recorded itself `other` 300+ times: its first words were a question, its folder was /home/user, its branch HEAD, and the `_orchestrator` post named another session (c79c7b98) for part of the evening. A later row from an older kit relabelled it `orchestrator` but dropped its 324 commands. Now the row reads what the session ran: `kit.py resume --role orchestrator`, `kit.py launch`/`land` (only the orchestrator does), or a write of the `_orchestrator` post; first prompt and branch still win when they name a role (a part stays a part).
- **Full-board pulls.** `artifact pull` already printed only changes after a first load, but every part starts in a fresh container: its first pull listed the whole board (posts ~10k characters, comments ~11.5k in the reply), and 12 of 12 parts did it. The guard let any list through whose `out_dir` was the pull's folder, so hand-made lists passed too.

### What changed
1. `usage.py`: `roles_run` from the transcript; `classify` uses it when nothing else names a role; `merge_rows` keeps an older row's command sequence and orchestrator label.
2. `kit.py artifact pull --post <id>` (and remembered from `resume --role part --post`): the post, `_orchestrator`, `_trains`, `_dashboard`, `_prefs`, the train's post by `get`, the post's comments by one `query`, the files' map. `--full` still lists all. Resume's attached-board line no longer prints a raw list.
3. `kit_orchestrator_guard.py`: a whole-collection read passes only if `artifact pull` printed it in the last 30 minutes (its record `pull.json`).
4. `usage.py audit [--since T] [--role R] [--top N] [--json]`; `resume --role orchestrator` prints the top 3; the orchestrator guide runs it at each Done and check-in.

### Measured on the real board (11-26)

|---|---|---|
| first pull, whole board (before) | 3 (2 lists + the map) | 22,252 |
| first pull of a part, `--post` (after) | 8 (6 gets, 1 query, the map) | 3,525 |
| a refused batch (before and after) | one `get` per document named | no list |

Carried: each result's tokens times the calls that followed it, at the cache read price. An ArtifactData call counts as the kit's when the command just before it was a kit script that printed it (pull, push, done, the takeover).
breaks: sed -i 's/    if rr:  # M11/    if False:  # M11/; s/    scope = "" if full or since else _scope_post(post)/    scope = ""/' scripts/usage.py scripts/kit.py
differs: M11: builds on M6's per-command ledger (it measures cost) and M7's K3 (reuse the kit's commands, unchecked): M11 turns them into a check that flags each manual action where a kit command exists, fixes the orchestrator's role label, and stops full-board reads in pulls and pins.
handoff:
- CR-m11 redirect done here: `pull.json` (version 2) records each printed call whole and the guard marks it used; `pending.json`, written by `artifact push` and removed by the last `artifact sent`, limits reads to `get` of its ids; a review's prompt says `artifact pull --post <post>`.
- Rows now carry `roles_run` and a note per result in `cmd_seq` ([command, carry $, result tokens, target]); `usage.py audit_row(row)` and `audit_top(rows)` read them.
- The part prompt says `kit.py artifact pull --post <id>`; `resume --role part --post X` also remembers X, so a plain first pull is scoped too. A review's prompt names `--post` too.
- `kit_orchestrator_guard.py` lets each `list` or broad `query` of posts/comments a pull printed through once (`.kit/run/artifact/pull.json`, 30 min).
- The orchestrator template now runs `kit.py usage audit --since ...` at each Done and each check-in; resume --role orchestrator prints the top 3 of the last 24 h.
not_checked: The guard's new wiring takes effect in sessions started after it (Claude Code reads the hook settings at start); this session ran the flow by hand, not under the hook.

Rows recorded before today's kit keep only each result's command name and carry: the audit cannot tell a `sed` of a board file from a `sed` of code there (file reads are flagged only on rows recorded from now on), and a `board_cli.py get` there is flagged as "target not recorded" (some are the prompt's own comment read).

The orchestrator's ledger row: a kit from before M6 (568b8f5, in another clone) rewrote it without a sequence; I pushed its earlier row through the new merge, so `usage audit --role orchestrator` now shows it (324 of its calls). If that old clone records again, it can overwrite the row again until it gets this kit (the Harmonize run).

The orchestrator's own first pull in a fresh container is still the whole board (it needs every post); after it, changes only. The review's row 3 is refused because its record lacks the whole call; the real "same list again" case is the single-use test.
On a computer, the role label still also comes from the `_orchestrator` post; not run on a computer here.

The guard is wired in .claude only (agy has no ArtifactData tool). Verdict: works.

task:
Every session uses the kit's own commands where one exists, the ledger shows when it does not, and the orchestrator is counted as the orchestrator.

Measured on 2026-11-26 (kit-usage rows, `kit.py usage show --commands`): the orchestrator session 9919b5f1 is labelled role `other`; it made 9 `ArtifactData list` calls of the whole board (116k chars) and parts made 31 (318k chars, 12 of 12 sessions), although `kit.py artifact pull` prints only what changed by default (`--full` for all). Parts read code with `sed` 99 times (507k chars). The orchestrator also read posts raw (`board_cli.py get` 15 times) and built pins by hand from full lists. Nobody checked whether sessions used the kit's commands.

1. The usage row labels the orchestrator `orchestrator` on the web and on a computer, whatever its start (the `_orchestrator` post's session_id, a hand-over, or a session that took over mid-way); a test with a transcript like 9919b5f1's.
2. Every full-board read goes through `kit.py artifact pull` (changes only); the pin and version-mismatch path re-reads only the documents it names (`get`/`query` by id), never a full `list`. Measure: the calls a pull and a refused batch print, before and after, on the real board.
3. `kit.py usage audit [--since T] [--role R]`: from the ledger's `cmd_seq`, lists each session's manual actions where a kit command exists (raw `ArtifactData list`/`get` of posts, `board_cli.py get`, `sed`/`cat` of board files, hand-built pins), with the command it should have used and the tokens it carried. The orchestrator runs it at each Done and at each check-in; resume --role orchestrator prints its top 3.
4. Run it on today's rows and put the table in the post.
title: Sessions use the kit's commands, the ledger shows when they don't, and the orchestrator is labelled as such
verdict: Yes: the role label comes from what the session ran, full-board reads go through the kit (refused otherwise), and the audit on today's 20 sessions puts first-pull full lists first: 48 calls, 10.5M tokens carried.
